title: Autorecover divergence detector & staged reconciliation for safe config applies
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Goal: Implement an automatic 'autorecover' subsystem that detects semantic divergence after config applies (batching/caching/kv-cache/prefetch policies) and executes a staged reconciliation that minimizes customer impact and cost while providing auditability and operator controls. The system should surface actionable signals, simulate safe roll-forward or staged revert plans, and optionally apply an automated rollback only when multi-signal guardrails trigger with confidence thresholds. This ticket covers design, implementation of the detector, integration with the state reconciliation engine, a lightweight policy DSL for guardrails, and observability hooks for post-apply validation.
acceptance_criteria: Divergence detector returns a probabilistic divergence score for config applies within 10s of rollout completion
Staged reconciliation can run a dry-run simulation that predicts token-cost delta and latency delta for up to 3 candidate actions
Automated rollback executes only when >=2 independent signals exceed configured thresholds and operator approval policy is met (can be configured to auto-approve for low-risk customers)
All actions are logged to audit stream with links to the causation configs, telemetry snapshots, and generated revert plan
Integration tests that inject controlled KV cache/ batching regressions and validate rollback path succeed in CI
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design proto - define signals (error rate, tail-latency, cost-per-req, cache-miss spike, prefix-loss), message schema, and thresholds (3 days)
Phase 2: Detector - implement sliding-window aggregators + Bayesian drift detector; expose API /internal/config-viz/divergence
Phase 3: Planer - build reconciliation planner that enumerates actions (revert toggle, scale-up, reduce-batch-size, quarantine-prefix) and simulates token/cost impact using historical traffic traces
Phase 4: Guardrail DSL - small YAML policy for combining signals, confidence levels, customer tiers and operator actions
Phase 5: Execution - wire safe-apply runner with canary gating, staged rollback steps, backoff and hysteresis
Phase 6: Observability - dashboards, audit events, runbooks and automated postmortem snippets
Phase 7: Testing & rollout - unit/integration/chaos tests, opt-in beta with 3 internal teams, GA rollout
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after oncall incident where a batching config change caused 35% cost spike for a production tenant (incident link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/INC-2026-03-batching-cost-spike)

2026-03-03: Architecture sync: decided on Bayesian drift detector + ensemble signals (latency P99, cost per token, cache miss rate, error spike). Trade-off: more signals increase uptime sensitivity; chosen conservative thresholds for P0 rollout
2026-03-05: Prototype implemented for sliding-window aggregator (proof-of-concept in ace/telemetry repo). Initial false-positive rate ~8% on historical traces
2026-03-07: PM review (Sofia Chen) requested clearer operator UX for manual override and a 'preview revert' that lists expected cost delta
2026-03-09: Design review: added staged reconciliation plan (simulate -> canary revert -> full revert) and a quarantine prefix step for KV-cache contamination
2026-03-10: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421 - detector + API stubs. Seeking eng review from @leo and @sanaa
2026-03-11: Load test with recorded traffic (console-perf replay) shows detector latency 6.2s and correctly flags the injected regression in 9/10 runs
2026-03-12: Security review check-in: feature flagged; will not auto-rollback for enterprise customers until KMS audit fields verified
risks: False positives could cause unnecessary rollbacks affecting availability
Simulators may not accurately predict regression magnitude for novel traffic patterns
Automated actions require strong audit trail to satisfy compliance for Private deployments
Interference with existing canary/rollout controllers if reconciliation and rollout share control without clear locking semantics
qa_plan: Create synthetic test harness to inject cache-miss spikes and batching size regressions
Add integration test that exercises guardrail DSL, verifies simulation outputs and ensures audit events emitted
Chaos experiment: toggle feature flag during heavy traffic window in staging and validate no customer-visible errors
Post-deploy canary with 0.5% traffic for 48 hours then gradually increase
rollout_strategy: Feature-flagged rollout: internal alpha -> select beta customers -> enterprise opt-in -> GA
Default behavior off for enterprise accounts; enable-by-request after security audit
Expose a 'simulate-only' mode for platform engineers to preview reconciliation plans without executing
